cards.title: Litter and public spaces
facts: Litter blocks drains and causes waterlogging in the monsoon.
People copy what they see others do, good or bad.
do: Keep the wrapper until you find a bin
Separate wet and dry waste
Politely encourage friends to do the same
dont: Don't drop litter even if others do
Don't throw things out of vehicle windows

myths.statement: One wrapper doesn't matter; it's the city's job to clean up.
myths.truth: Millions of 'just one wrapper' block drains. Everyone shares the job.

quiz.q: There's no dustbin on the bus. What do you do with your wrapper?
options: Throw it out of the window
Keep it in your bag until you find a bin
quiz.explanation: Fold it into your bag and bin it later.

situations: {name} finishes a packet of chips {at}. There's no dustbin anywhere, and {relation} says 'Just drop it under the seat, everyone does.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Keep the wrapper until finding a bin
rubric.note: Fold it into a pocket or bag and bin it later.

rubric.point: Don't drop it, even if 'everyone does'
rubric.note: The right thing doesn't depend on others.

rubric.point: Politely encourage the friend too

cards.title: Queues and public transport
facts: Letting people off first makes boarding faster for everyone.
Priority seats are for elderly, pregnant, disabled people and parents with small children.
do: Wait your turn in the queue
Let passengers get off before boarding
Offer your seat to someone who needs it more
Keep bags off seats
dont: Don't push or cut the queue
Don't play loud music without headphones

myths.statement: Priority seats are only for people who ask for them.
myths.truth: Offer them without being asked. Many people won't ask.

quiz.q: The metro doors open and the train is crowded. What first?
quiz.explanation: Letting people off first makes boarding faster for everyone.

situations: {name} has just got the last seat on a crowded bus. At the next stop, an elderly woman with a heavy bag gets on and holds the rail. {relation} whispers 'Pretend you're asleep.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Offer the seat politely
rubric.note: Offer without waiting to be asked.

rubric.point: Help with the bag if she wants
rubric.note: Small help goes a long way.

rubric.point: Not pretend to sleep / set a good example

cards.title: Finding a lost child
facts: Lost children should be handed to officials such as security, police or staff, not taken home.
1098 is CHILDLINE, India's free helpline for children in need.
do: Stay with the child in a busy, visible place
Tell security, a shop counter or police
Ask for an announcement
dont: Don't take the child home or away from the area
Don't post their photo online

myths.statement: If you find a lost child, it's best to take them home and look after them.
myths.truth: Hand them to security, staff or police at the spot, where parents will search.

quiz.q: You find a crying child alone in a mall. Best step?
options: Stay with them and tell security or staff
quiz.explanation: Staff can make announcements, and parents will come back to that area.

cards.title: Caring for public property
facts: Public property is paid for by everyone's taxes.
Leaking public taps can waste thousands of litres.
do: Report damage or leaks to the authority or school
Close running public taps
Use walls and benches as they're meant to be used
dont: Don't scribble on walls or monuments
Don't damage benches, signs or plants

myths.statement: Writing your name on a monument is harmless fun.
myths.truth: It damages heritage that belongs to everyone, and it's an offence.

quiz.q: You see a public tap left running. What do you do?
options: Close it, and report it if it's broken
quiz.explanation: Close it and report broken taps so they get fixed.

cards.title: Public spitting, paan stains and respiratory disease spread
facts: Saliva and sputum droplets carry bacteria (like Mycobacterium tuberculosis) that remain airborne for hours.
Public spitting disfigures sidewalks and walls and is a punishable offense under municipal civic bylaws.
do: Always spit into a tissue paper and dispose of it in a closed waste bin
Rinse mouth in dedicated washbasin sinks, not on walls or staircases
Remind family and peers that spitting spreads tuberculosis and respiratory infections
dont: Never spit on footpaths, roads, bus stops, or building stairwells
Never spit out of moving buses or car windows

myths.statement: Spitting paan or tobacco on public walls is harmless once it dries.
myths.truth: Dried sputum particles get kicked up as infectious dust that passersby inhale into their lungs.

quiz.q: Why is public spitting strictly prohibited on roads, metro stations, and public spaces?
options: It spreads deadly airborne diseases like Tuberculosis and damages public hygiene
quiz.explanation: Spitting transmits infectious respiratory bacteria and viruses to everyone nearby.

situations: Walking through a bus station at {at}, {name} sees someone about to spit paan onto the wall.
scenario.question: How can {name} promote responsible civic cleanliness?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely remind that public spitting spreads diseases and spoils shared spaces
Use designated washroom sinks or spit into a tissue for the dustbin
Lead by personal example and never spit on shared streets

cards.title: Noise pollution: Honking, loudspeakers and silent zones
facts: Prolonged exposure to noise above 85 decibels causes permanent sensorineural hearing loss.
Hospitals, courts, and educational institutions are designated Silent Zones (no honking allowed within 100m).
do: Avoid honking vehicle horns unless preventing an imminent collision
Keep personal headphones and portable speaker volumes moderate in public transport
Respect night-time silence rules: no loud speakers after 10 PM near residential areas
dont: Never honk near hospital ICUs, old-age homes, or school exam centres
Never blast party speakers into midnight disturbing studying neighbours

myths.statement: Continuous honking in a traffic jam makes the vehicles in front move faster.
myths.truth: Honking does not clear stopped traffic; it causes intense acoustic stress and road rage.

quiz.q: Why is honking completely prohibited within 100 meters of a hospital?
options: Sudden loud acoustic spikes trigger cardiac stress and disturb critical patients
quiz.explanation: Noise spikes induce dangerous stress and sleep deprivation in ICU patients.

situations: A driver behind {name}'s school van at {at} is leaning on their horn right outside a hospital gate.
scenario.question: What civic rule should road users remember?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Hospitals are 24/7 Silent Zones where honking is strictly illegal
rubric.note: Protects recovering patients from acoustic shock.

rubric.point: Honking does not magically clear red lights or traffic bottlenecks
Keep noise low and respect quiet hours in residential neighbourhoods

sources.name: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) Noise Rules

cards.title: Respectful assistance for visually impaired citizens
facts: People with visual impairment navigate using white canes, tactile pavings, and auditory landmarks.
Grabbing someone's arm or cane unexpectedly without asking startles and disorients them.
do: Always ask first: 'Hello, may I help you cross the road or find the platform?'
Offer your elbow for them to hold lightly; walk a half-step ahead at a natural pace
Verbally describe steps, curbs, and hazards clearly (e.g. 'Step down in two steps')
dont: Never grab someone's white cane or pull them by the wrist
Never pet or distract a working guide dog

myths.statement: You should grab a blind person's hand and pull them across the road without talking.
myths.truth: Grabbing people without consent causes fear and loss of balance. Ask first, offer elbow.

quiz.q: How should you offer physical guidance to a visually impaired person crossing a street?
options: Ask first, then offer your elbow for them to hold as you walk
quiz.explanation: Holding your elbow allows them to follow your body movement smoothly and safely.

situations: Near a busy road crossing at {at}, {name} sees a person with a white cane waiting by the curb.
scenario.question: How should {name} offer assistance respectfully?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Greet them politely and ask: 'Hello, would you like assistance crossing the street?'
If they accept, offer your elbow and guide them smoothly
Describe curbs and steps clearly: 'Curb step down right now'

sources.name: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

cards.title: Giving immediate right-of-way to emergency ambulances
facts: Every second lost in transit reduces survival odds for heart attack and trauma victims.
Failing to give way to emergency vehicles attracts a fine of up to ₹10,000 under the Motor Vehicles Act.
do: Move your vehicle or cycle immediately to the left side of the road when a siren sounds
Clear the center lane or create an emergency green corridor
Never tail or closely follow an ambulance to zip through cleared traffic
dont: Never block or race an ambulance with flashing lights and sirens
Never freeze in the middle of an intersection

myths.statement: Following right behind a rushing ambulance is a smart shortcut to bypass city traffic.
myths.truth: Tailgating ambulances causes rear-end crashes and obstructs emergency braking.

quiz.q: What should all vehicles immediately do when an ambulance siren is heard approaching from behind?
options: Safely pull over to the left to open a clear lane
Stop dead in the middle lane
quiz.explanation: Pulling to the left creates a continuous open emergency corridor for critical patients.

situations: Riding on the road at {at}, an ambulance siren blares loudly behind {name}'s vehicle.
scenario.question: What is the immediate legal and moral civic duty?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Safely maneuver to the left side of the road to clear the path
rubric.note: Opens a clear channel for emergency transit.
rubric.keys: pull to left|clear path|move aside|give way

rubric.point: Encourage other drivers to yield right-of-way
Never tailgate behind the ambulance to skip signals

cards.title: Treating sanitation workers, security guards and domestic staff with dignity
facts: Sanitation workers, housekeeping staff, and security guards keep our cities functional and safe.
Article 14 and 21 of the Indian Constitution uphold equal human dignity for every citizen.
do: Greet service staff with a warm 'Namaste', 'Good morning', or 'Thank you'
Address domestic workers, bus conductors, and guards with polite respectful honorifics (Bhaiya, Didi, Uncle)
Offer drinking water to delivery agents and cleaners visiting your building
dont: Never speak rudely, snap fingers, or look down upon manual laborers
Never leave broken glass unseparated in trash that can cut waste collectors' hands

myths.statement: You only need to show respect to rich professionals, not sanitation workers.
myths.truth: Dignity of labor is the bedrock of civilized society. Every honest job deserves deep respect.

quiz.q: What is the simplest everyday habit that shows civic respect to your apartment security guard?
options: A polite greeting, acknowledging their work, and saying 'Thank you'
quiz.explanation: Simple everyday courtesy validates the dignity and contribution of essential service staff.

situations: A delivery partner climbs three flights of stairs in hot weather at {at} to hand over a package.
scenario.question: What civic courtesy should {name} extend?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Receive package with a warm 'Thank you' and offer a glass of clean water
rubric.note: Demonstrates genuine human warmth and empathy.

rubric.point: Speak with respect and patience without snapping or arrogance
Recognize their hard work keeping city logistics moving

cards.title: Buffet discipline and zero food waste at weddings and parties
facts: Thousands of tons of edible food are dumped into garbage pits after lavish weddings every night.
Unattended heaps of wasted food on dirty paper plates attract stray pests and rot.
do: Take small initial portions at wedding buffets; you can revisit counters freely
Only pick dishes you genuinely intend to eat rather than trying to taste everything on one plate
Encourage hosts to partner with food rescue NGOs (like Robin Hood Army) to distribute surplus untouched food
dont: Never pile mountains of halwa and biryani only to abandon half-eaten plates
Never throw whole untouched food packets into garden hedges

myths.statement: Leaving half your wedding buffet plate unconsumed is standard high-class etiquette.
myths.truth: Wasting food while millions face hunger is deeply insensitive and un-civic.

quiz.q: You are at a wedding reception buffet with 20 delicious dishes. What is the smart, civic way to eat?
options: Heap all 20 dishes onto one plate so it overflows
Take 2-3 dishes you really enjoy in small portions, and return for seconds if hungry
quiz.explanation: Taking modest portions avoids wasting food and lets you enjoy meals fresher.

situations: At a family wedding function at {at}, {name} is at the dessert buffet counter.
scenario.question: What is the responsible civic approach?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take small portions of one or two treats you will actually finish
rubric.keys: small portion|take what you finish|one treat

rubric.point: Do not leave half-eaten desserts on chairs or ledges
If surplus untouched food remains, suggest donating to verified food charities

sources.name: Robin Hood Army & Feeding India Guidelines

cards.title: Closing leaking public taps and reporting pipeline bursts
facts: A single faucet dripping one drop per second wastes over 3,000 litres of treated water every year.
Clean drinking water is an increasingly scarce natural resource in Indian cities.
do: Close any running or half-open public tap you see at railway stations, parks, or schools
Place a bucket underneath while alerting facility maintenance if a tap cannot be shut fully
Report major street pipeline bursts on municipal citizen grievance helplines
dont: Never walk past a gushing municipal drinking tap without taking action
Never leave school washroom taps running while soaping hands

myths.statement: A leaking tap in a public park is the government's problem, not a citizen's concern.
myths.truth: Public water belongs to all citizens. Closing running taps is a direct civic duty.

quiz.q: What should you do if you notice a drinking water tap running freely at a train station?
options: Stop for 5 seconds and turn the tap handle fully closed
Complain on social media without closing it
quiz.explanation: Taking 5 seconds to close the tap saves hundreds of litres of clean drinking water.

situations: At the public park or sports ground at {at}, a drinking water fountain tap is left gushing full blast.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Step up and turn the tap firmly clockwise until the water flow stops completely
If the washer is broken, report the leak to the park supervisor or maintenance staff
Remind peers to turn off taps while brushing or applying soap

cards.title: Responsible pet walking: Leashes, scooping and colony courtesy
facts: Dog waste contains harmful bacteria (Campylobacter, Salmonella) and parasite eggs that contaminate shoes.
Unleashed pet dogs can startle young children, elderly strollers, or provoke territorial street dogs.
do: Always keep your pet dog on a secure, comfortable leash in public society areas and parks
Carry old newspapers, plastic bags, or a poop-scooper to clean up your pet's waste immediately
Ensure pets are up-to-date on yearly anti-rabies vaccinations and society registration
dont: Never leave your pet's waste on common walking tracks, flowerbeds, or building corridors
Never allow pets to jump onto unwilling neighbors or strangers

myths.statement: Leaving dog poop on public pavements is fine because it dissolves in rain naturally.
myths.truth: Pavement feces spread diseases to children, soil shoes, and ruin common hygiene.

quiz.q: What must a responsible pet parent always carry when walking their dog in a society park?
options: A sturdy leash and a bag or scooper to pick up pet waste
quiz.explanation: Leashing ensures control and waste bags keep neighborhood walking tracks spotless.

situations: Walking a family pet in the colony garden at {at}, the dog relieves itself near the jogging track.
scenario.question: What is {name}'s civic obligation as a pet guardian?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Use a bag or paper to pick up the waste and deposit it in an outdoor garbage bin
Keep the dog on a secure leash at all times in common areas
rubric.note: Prevents unexpected jumps on elderly neighbors.

rubric.point: Respect neighbors who may feel anxious around unfamiliar dogs

sources.name: Animal Welfare Board Guidelines on Pet Dogs in Resident Welfare Associations

cards.title: Respecting shared spaces: Corridors, elevators and parks
facts: Corridors and stairwells are primary emergency fire evacuation corridors that must stay 100% clear.
Dumping personal shoes, bicycles, and flowerpots in common corridors creates dangerous trip hazards.
do: Keep shared stairwells and lift lobbies free of personal junk, old furniture, and garbage bags
Hold the elevator door politely for approaching residents carrying groceries or prams
Dispose of personal snack wrappers in outdoor dustbins, never leaving them on park benches
dont: Never leave leaky garbage bags leaking smelly liquid in shared elevator lobbies
Never scribble graffiti or stick chewing gum inside common lifts

myths.statement: Corridors outside your apartment door belong exclusively to your flat to store clutter.
myths.truth: Common corridors are shared community property and legal fire escape routes.

quiz.q: Why must building stairwells and common corridors always be kept completely clear of clutter?
options: They are emergency fire evacuation routes that people must navigate in smoke and darkness
quiz.explanation: Blocked staircases cause lethal crush injuries and trapped residents during night fire alarms.

situations: In the apartment building at {at}, someone has dumped old broken bicycles and boxes in the stairwell.
scenario.question: What civic issue does {name} recognize?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stairwells are emergency fire escape routes that must remain completely unobstructed
Common spaces belong to all residents and should be kept tidy and clean
Notify the Resident Welfare Association (RWA) or building committee to clear the blockage

sources.name: Model Bye-Laws for Resident Welfare Associations

cards.title: From bystander to upstander: Standing up against teasing
facts: Bullying thrives when surrounding peers remain silent, which bullies interpret as approval.
Research shows that when a single peer intervenes kindly, over 50% of bullying stops within 10 seconds.
do: Stand next to the targeted student and invite them away: 'Come on, let's go play basketball together'
Speak clearly to the teaser: 'That's not funny, let's stop this'
Report persistent bullying to a trusted teacher or school counselor
dont: Never join in laughing or filming teasing videos on mobile phones
Never resort to physical violence or aggressive insults to solve conflict

myths.statement: Watching someone get teased without saying anything means you are neutral and innocent.
myths.truth: Passive silence empowers the bully. An upstander uses gentle words to support the victim.

quiz.q: What is the most effective way a student can act as an 'upstander' when a classmate is mocked?
options: Step in, support the classmate, and invite them away to a safe spot
Film a video for social media
quiz.explanation: Distracting the situation and supporting the victim dissolves the bully's audience.

situations: In the school courtyard at {at}, two older students are mocking a classmate's accent and laughing.
scenario.question: How can {name} act as a courageous civic upstander?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Walk up to the classmate and warmly invite them to join your group
rubric.note: Removes the victim from the aggressive interaction.

rubric.point: Clearly say: 'Hey, that's unkind, let's stop this' without getting aggressive
Inform a teacher if the teasing persists or turns physical

cards.title: Preserving historical monuments and stopping graffiti vandalism
facts: Ancient stone monuments and forts represent irreplaceable centuries-old national architecture.
Scratching names or painting graffiti on protected archaeological sites is a crime under AMASR Act.
do: Admire historical monuments with eyes and cameras without touching delicate carvings
Follow all ASI site rules: carry waste back with you and stay within marked visitor ropes
Speak up politely if friends pull out keys or markers to scratch graffiti on ancient walls
dont: Never carve or scratch initials ('Raju loves Priya') into ancient stone or bricks
Never discard plastic bottles, wrappers, or chewing gum inside heritage compounds

myths.statement: Scratching your name onto an ancient fort wall is a harmless romantic tradition.
myths.truth: Carving scratches off the protective mineral patina, accelerating chemical weathering and stone crumbling.

quiz.q: What law protects Indian historical monuments from graffiti, defacement, and destruction?
options: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act
quiz.explanation: The AMASR Act makes defacing historical monuments punishable by fines and imprisonment.

situations: On a school excursion to a historical monument at {at}, a classmate takes out a coin to carve initials on a stone pillar.
scenario.question: What should {name} tell them immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Firmly stop them: 'Please don't carve on ancient stone, it permanently ruins centuries of heritage'
Remind them that defacing monuments is an illegal offense under archaeological laws
Keep our shared cultural heritage pristine for future generations

cards.title: Reporting civic problems on municipal apps (potholes, streetlights)
facts: Municipal corporations in India have dedicated grievance apps (Swachhata, MyGov, local Smart City portals).
Geo-tagged citizen photo reports automatically route repair work orders to local ward engineers.
do: Download and use your city's municipal grievance app (e.g. Swachhata-MoHUA or city corporation app)
Take a clear, geotagged photo showing the broken streetlight, open pothole, or garbage dump
Track the complaint ticket number until the municipal authority marks it resolved with an 'after' photo
dont: Never submit fake, abusive, or duplicate frivolous complaint tickets
Never ignore severe public hazards (like open electric junction boxes) without reporting

myths.statement: Filing municipal complaints online is useless because nobody ever checks civic apps.
myths.truth: Swachhata and Smart City portals have mandatory time-bound SLAs monitored by municipal commissioners.

quiz.q: What feature in citizen grievance apps ensures municipal workers find the exact location of a pothole?
options: GPS geotagging embedded in the submitted photograph
quiz.explanation: Geotagged photos pinpoint exact latitude/longitude coordinates for engineering crews.

situations: Outside school at {at}, a deep road pothole fills with water, creating an accident hazard for cyclists.
scenario.question: How can {name} and their family take constructive civic action?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take a clear geotagged photo using the official municipal grievance app
rubric.note: Initiates an official traceable civic repair ticket.

rubric.point: Provide the exact street name and prominent landmark in the description
rubric.note: Enables ward staff to locate the pothole easily.

rubric.point: Track the complaint ticket until the road repair is completed

sources.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

cards.title: Why voting and Fundamental Duties matter for every citizen
facts: Democracy thrives on active, informed citizen participation, not passive cynicism.
Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists 11 Fundamental Duties, including protecting public property and the environment.
do: Learn how local elections function (ward corporators, MLAs, MPs) and how budgets are spent
Encourage eligible adult family members to register and vote in every single election
Fulfill student fundamental duties: protect the environment, respect the national flag, and develop scientific temper
dont: Never treat voting day as just a leisure picnic holiday
Never trade votes for money, gifts, or communal pressure

myths.statement: A single citizen's vote makes zero difference in a country of 1.4 billion people.
myths.truth: Crucial elections have been won or lost by a single vote. Every vote shapes governance and schools.

quiz.q: Where are the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens listed in the Constitution?
quiz.explanation: Article 51A outlines citizen duties toward the nation, public property, and nature.

situations: Election day approaches in the city at {at}, and {name}'s family considers skipping voting to go to the mall.
scenario.question: What democratic perspective should {name} share?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Voting is a democratic right and duty that determines our roads, schools, and hospitals
rubric.note: Connects voting to quality of public life.
rubric.keys: duty to vote|democracy|vote matters|elect good leaders

rubric.point: Encourage every eligible adult in the family to exercise their constitutional franchise
Remember that student fundamental duties include developing a rational scientific temper

cards.title: Decorum, courtesy and quiet respect in places of worship
facts: Temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras, and viharas are sanctified spaces for quiet contemplation.
Respecting diverse traditions (removing shoes, covering heads, turning off phones) fosters interfaith peace.
do: Turn mobile phones completely to silent or switch them off before entering any place of worship
Follow traditional dress and entry customs respectfully (cover head, remove footwear, wash feet)
Maintain quiet speaking tones and refrain from running or shouting inside prayer halls
dont: Never take intrusive flash photography or selfies in front of praying worshippers
Never mock or disrespect sacred symbols or rituals of other communities

myths.statement: It is acceptable to answer loud phone calls in a temple or church if it's an important video game update.
myths.truth: Prayer spaces are sanctuaries of peace. Loud phone chatter is deeply disruptive and disrespectful.

quiz.q: What is the first thing you should do with your mobile phone before entering a place of worship?
options: Switch it to silent mode or turn it off completely
quiz.explanation: Silencing phones preserves the tranquil spiritual atmosphere for all visitors.

situations: Visiting an ancient temple, gurdwara, or church at {at}, {name} enters the quiet prayer hall.
scenario.question: What respectful decorum should {name} uphold?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Silence mobile phone and speak only in gentle whisper tones
Respect site-specific customs like removing shoes or covering head
Do not disturb praying devotees with flash selfies or videos

cards.title: Prioritizing the elderly, pregnant women and disabled in public queues
facts: Standing for extended periods causes painful joint stress for elderly and pregnant citizens.
Designated priority seats and ticket counters ensure equitable access to basic public infrastructure.
do: Offer your seat immediately to elderly passengers, pregnant women, or people with infants on buses/metros
Allow seniors or persons with mobility aids to move ahead in ticket, billing, or clinic queues
Queue in an orderly single-file line without jumping spots or cutting in front of others
dont: Never pretend to be asleep in designated 'Senior Citizen' seats to avoid standing
Never shove past slow-walking elderly commuters on escalators or stairs

myths.statement: Pretending to sleep in a metro priority seat is a smart way to keep your seat.
myths.truth: Feigning sleep to deprive elderly or pregnant citizens of seats shows a severe lack of empathy.

quiz.q: You are seated on a crowded metro and an elderly person with a cane boards. What should you do?
options: Close your eyes and pretend to sleep
Stand up immediately, smile, and offer them your seat
quiz.explanation: Offering your seat to seniors demonstrates basic civic compassion and respect.

situations: In a long queue at a medical dispensary or metro counter at {at}, an elderly person with a walking stick joins the back of the line.
scenario.question: How can {name} exhibit exemplary civic kindness?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Smile and offer to let the senior person move ahead in the queue
rubric.note: Shows active consideration for physical vulnerability.
rubric.keys: let move ahead|offer spot|priority queue|seniors first

rubric.point: Offer your seat if on a bus or metro train
rubric.note: Protects fragile commuters from falling during transit.

rubric.point: Maintain orderly queue discipline without pushing or cutting lines

sources.name: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

cards.title: Everyday gratitude to community helpers and municipal crews
facts: A community that values its service workers fosters higher social happiness and civic pride.
Expressing genuine verbal appreciation ('Thank you for your service') transforms working morale.
do: Thank your school bus driver and conductor when stepping down every afternoon
Say a heartfelt 'Thank you' to street sweepers and garbage collectors working in your lane
Keep your own classroom desks and school cafeteria tables neat to lighten helper workloads
dont: Never treat cleaners as invisible or treat their service as something to take for granted
Never litter on grounds right in front of someone sweeping

myths.statement: Saying 'Thank you' to sanitation workers or bus conductors is unnecessary because they get paid.
myths.truth: Compensation pays for work; human gratitude and courtesy validate human dignity.

quiz.q: What is the simplest way to show everyday gratitude to your school bus driver at the end of the day?
options: Smile and say: 'Thank you Bhaiya/Uncle, have a good evening!'
Leave candy wrappers on the floor
quiz.explanation: A warm, respectful verbal thank you acknowledges their responsibility for your safety.

situations: At school dismissal at {at}, {name} steps off the bus after a safe journey home.
scenario.question: What closing civic gesture should {name} make?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Look at the driver and conductor, smile, and say: 'Thank you for the safe ride!'
rubric.note: Recognizes essential daily service with warmth.

rubric.point: Pick up any personal snack wrappers or trash from your seat
rubric.note: Keeps the shared vehicle tidy for tomorrow.

rubric.point: Extend the same everyday kindness to all community workers

sources.name: Department of School Education and Literacy (Civic Values)
